title: observability: token-level logging + KV metrics + tracing dashboard + alert tuning
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Improve token-level observability for hybrid workloads by adding structured token logging, KV-cache metrics, and end-to-end tracing joins in the unified observability dashboards. This addresses gaps surfaced during load testing and a recent post-incident review where per-token cost spikes could not be reliably attributed to cache behavior or routing fallbacks. Summary of changes: - Add structured token-level logs (JSON) emitted by the runtime with deterministic fields (request_id, model, variant, token_index, token_type, latency_ms, cache_hit) - Expose KV-cache metrics (per-model kv_hits, kv_misses, kv_evictions, kv_hit_ratio) in Prometheus format and wire them into existing metrics exporter - Add distributed tracing spans in the runtime hot path to correlate token generation latencies with KV lookups and routing decisions - New Grafana dashboard (observability/token-level-kv-tracing) combining cost-per-token, latency percentiles, KV hit heatmaps, and trace-links - Alert tuning: add two new alerts and adjust thresholds for existing token-latency alerts to reduce noisiness on routine bursts - Add migration script and docs for enabling token logs and sample dashboards (Console + Grafana) Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for new metrics + log schema - [x] Integration tests for trace propagation across runtime -> router -> storage - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + dashboard provisioning changes - [x] Docs + Console quickstart (feature flag) - [x] Perf run (benchmark-lab) showing <3% median latency regression for 2048-length workloads Rollout plan: feature-flag the token logs and KV metrics by default-off; enable for internal Dedicated clusters for 1 week, then ramp to 10% hosted traffic, monitor token-cost and latency SLOs, then full rollout. If KV hit ratio regressions observed, automatic rollback to previous exporter version. Backwards compatibility: dashboard provisioning is additive; token logs are opt-in and do not change existing log formats unless enabled. Release notes: See release_notes field. Testing: local unit tests, CI integration tests, end-to-end smoke with sample workloads, perf runs on perf-canary. Related: ENG-1982, PM-453, SUP-2211, and follow-up doc in redwood-docs#observability-token-level
commits: 3 commits: 1) Add token logging schema + structured emitter; 2) KV metrics exporter + instrumentation; 3) Grafana dashboard + alert rules + docs
diff_snippets: runtime/logging/token_emitter.go: emit JSON lines with fields {request_id, model, variant, token_index, token_text, token_type, latency_ms, cache_hit}. exporter/prometheus/exporter.go: add kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_misses_total, kv_cache_evictions_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio gauge set. observability/alerts/token_latency_rules.yaml: loosened token_latency_p99 alert for short-lived bursts; added token_kv_miss_spike and token_cost_spike alerts.
review_comments: Evan Miller: Can we avoid serializing the full token_text to logs by default? Suggestions: sample or hash token_text. - Reply (Priya): agreed; token_text is sampled by default, full_text available behind flag.
Sofia Chen: Alert thresholds look sane but let's add a 5-minute mute window for expected scheduled load tests. - Reply (Priya): added a silence rule and documented in rollout plan.

Liam O'Connor: Need to ensure trace context is propagated for cross-region routing. Observability team will run a cross-region smoke. - Reply (Priya): traced propagation tests added to CI; included example for router/span correlation.
QA (Jordan Lee): Integration tests flaked initially due to timing; increased test timeouts and made assertions tolerant to minor jitter.
incident_notes: This PR was motivated by a minor incident on 2025-09-30 where token-cost spikes were observed in hosted region us-east-1. The postmortem recommended improved token-level visibility and KV metrics to identify cold-cache routing behavior.
perf_summary: Perf (benchmark-lab): ran 5k requests at 2048-length mixed traffic. Median latency regression 2.7%, p99 unchanged. KV hit ratio improved by 1.8% in workloads that used prefix caching. CPU/GPU utilization within expected bounds.
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged: disable token logs + metrics exporter and redeploy exporter container; Grafana changes are additive; rollback steps documented in docs/observability/token-level.md
release_notes: Observability: Add opt-in token-level logs, KV-cache metrics, and a new Grafana dashboard that correlates per-token latency with KV cache behavior and traces. Includes new alerts for KV miss spikes and token-cost spikes; opt-in by default for 1.0 release.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in Dedicated clusters, watch kv_cache_hit_ratio and token_kv_miss_spike alert for first 24 hours. Increase ingestion retention to avoid high-cardinality issues; recommended retention 7d for token logs during ramp.
